datasets.method: The multiple is median home value divided by median household income, county by county. A county is shown as confidently above 5x only when its whole margin of error (90%, approximate) is above 5, and confidently below only when the whole margin is below; otherwise it is uncertain. The margin of a ratio of two medians is the Census's approximation formula, not a published Census interval.

derivations.measure: Home value to household income (the multiple)
derivations.method: median home value divided by median household income, per county and per five-year window

breaks.what: Connecticut's eight counties are replaced by nine planning regions, and Alaska's Valdez-Cordova area is split into the Chugach and Copper River areas. Each window is drawn on its own published map; nothing is converted between them, so those areas are not comparable across the change.

measures.label: Median home value to median household income, by county

read: Home value is the owners' own estimate of what their home is worth. It is not a sale price.
Income is the median for all households in the county, before taxes. Homes and households are different groups, so this is a ratio of two medians, not what a buyer earns or can borrow.
Each frame is a five-year survey window, not a single year. The film shows four windows; nothing is drawn between them.
5x is our storytelling line, not an official standard.

Plain grey means the Census has no usable number for that county. Hatched grey (diagonal lines) means the margin of error is more than 30% of the multiple, so the county is too uncertain to call; it is never coloured by a band. Neither is ever drawn as zero.
The counter counts counties confidently above 5x. It is not a share of Americans or of homes.
The 2020-2024 window includes the pandemic years.
